title: Optimizing Pump Conditions of Parametric Amplifiers for Fast Multiplexed Readout of Superconducting Qubits
authors: Jeongwon Kim, Wei Dai, Omrie Ovdat, Akiva Feintuch, Nir Alfasi, Yonuk Chong
abstract: Low-noise parametric amplifiers are widely used as the first-stage amplifier in qubit readout chains. The performance of parametric amplifiers depends sensitively on the choice of the pump condition. We propose a strategy for determining the pump condition that is tailored for fast multiplexed readout. Choosing the amplifier pump to maximize the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improvement at the readout frequency of the limiting qubit--the qubit that requires the longest readout time to reach a target SNR--minimizes the total multiplexed readout time. We demonstrate our pump calibration strategy experimentally on a five-qubit multiplexed readout chain with a traveling-wave parametric amplifier. Using our strategy, we reduce the multiplexed readout time by 320 ns compared to optimizing the average SNR improvement on all qubits, without degrading the target SNR for any qubit.
summary: The research addresses how to optimize parametric amplifiers for fast, multi-qubit readout of superconducting qubits. The authors propose a novel strategy that prioritizes improving the performance of the single slowest qubit channel (the bottleneck). This approach experimentally demonstrated a significant reduction in overall readout time compared to optimizing for average performance across all qubits.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a pump optimization strategy for parametric amplifiers used in superconducting qubit readout chains to minimize the total multiplexed readout time.
main_result: By optimizing the amplifier pump condition based on the limiting (slowest) qubit channel rather than the average SNR, the authors achieved a significant reduction in the overall multiplexed readout time (e.g., 25% reduction).
method: The study experimentally calibrates the parametric amplifier by sweeping its frequency and power while comparing two optimization metrics: maximizing average $\Delta	ext{SNR}$ versus maximizing $\Delta	ext{SNR}$ for the bottleneck qubit.
model_or_system: The system involves superconducting qubits (e.g., five tunable transmon qubits) whose readout signals are amplified by a Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier (TWPA). The performance is governed by the interplay between amplifier gain, noise, and qubit relaxation times ($T_1$).
key_observables: Multiplexed Readout Time ($T_{	ext{MPX}}^{	ext{RO}}$), Signal-to-Noise Ratio ($	ext{SNR}$), $\Delta	ext{SNR}$, and required readout time ($	ext{TRO}$) for individual qubits.
important_parameters: Target SNR of 3 is chosen as the optimal point where further SNR improvement yields diminishing returns due to $T_1$ relaxation; the limiting qubit dictates $T_{	ext{MPX}}^{	ext{RO}}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that setting a fixed target $	ext{SNR}$ (e.g., 3) is optimal because increasing it further does not improve fidelity due to relaxation effects, and that readout time is limited by the slowest channel.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how different pump conditions affect gain profiles across multiple qubits; one figure compares the required readout times ($	ext{TRO}$) for both optimization strategies, showing a clear reduction in $T_{	ext{MPX}}^{	ext{RO}}$ when targeting the limiting qubit.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of minimizing multiplexed readout time set by the slowest channel. It then compares conventional average-optimization against the proposed limiting-channel optimization strategy, demonstrating quantitative improvements using experimental measurements on a multi-qubit array.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems because it tackles practical engineering constraints (readout speed) in superconducting circuits by optimizing the coupling element (parametric amplifier) based on system bottlenecks rather than simple averages.
